title: HTML5 and Modern Web Structure
subtitle: Modern features that complete your webpage for deployment
description: Master HTML5 modern elements: meta tags for SEO and social sharing, details/summary FAQ, dialog modal, datalist autocomplete, progress/meter, iframe embeds, HTML entities, data attributes, and prepare your complete webpage for real deployment.

blocks.text: Your webpage is good - now make it modern and deployable

You have built 70% of a complete webpage - semantic, with forms, images, tables. But open any modern site and you see FAQ that expands, modals, progress bars, autocomplete search, embedded maps and YouTube videos, rich previews when shared on WhatsApp. These are HTML5 modern features. Today we add them and also learn meta tags that make your webpage discoverable and shareable - essential for deployment.
Open Menu > Practical. We will upgrade your index.html with everything a modern complete webpage needs before deployment in Lesson 10.
Meta tags - invisible but decide if your webpage is found and shared

Meta tags live in head, user never sees them but Google and WhatsApp/Facebook/Twitter do. You know charset and viewport, but production webpages need description for Google snippet, author, Open Graph og:title, og:description, og:image for rich preview when shared on WhatsApp, Twitter card tags, and theme-color for mobile browser bar. Without these, your complete webpage will look broken when shared.

blocks.text: Details and Summary - native FAQ accordion without JavaScript

Every complete webpage needs FAQ. Old way needed JavaScript. HTML5 gives you details and summary - native expand/collapse. summary is the visible question, details wraps answer and toggles open/closed. Add open attribute to keep it open by default. This is accessible by default, keyboard works, screen readers announce expanded state.

blocks.text: Datalist, Progress, Meter, Output - small tags big UX

These tags were missing in earlier lessons but every modern webpage uses them. datalist gives autocomplete suggestions for input - like search suggestions. progress shows completion like course progress 70%. meter shows measurement like skill level. output shows result of calculation. All semantic and accessible.

blocks.text: Dialog and Iframe - modals and embeds for complete webpage

Dialog is HTML5 native modal - no JavaScript library needed. Use open attribute or showModal() with JS. For embeds like Google Maps, YouTube videos, Google Forms, use iframe. Critical iframe attributes: title for accessibility (mandatory), loading="lazy" for performance, sandbox for security to restrict what embedded page can do, allow for permissions.

blocks.text: Entities, Data Attributes, Template - last must-knows

Three more things every developer must know before final build: HTML Entities like < > & ©   for showing < > & characters without breaking HTML. Data attributes data-* for storing custom data for JavaScript - like data-price="500" data-project-id="123". Template tag for holding HTML that is not rendered but can be cloned by JavaScript for dynamic webpages.

blocks.question: You share your webpage link on WhatsApp and it shows only URL, no image or description. Another dev's link shows rich preview with image, title, description. What is missing in your head?
options: Missing <title> tag, title is what WhatsApp uses for preview image and description

Missing Open Graph meta tags og:title, og:description, og:image and twitter:card meta tags - these control rich preview when shared on social media and messaging apps, while description meta controls Google snippet
Missing tag in body, WhatsApp picks first image from body for preview, so need image at top of body
Missing alt attribute on images, WhatsApp uses alt text for preview description
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! OG tags are mandatory for professional complete webpages that will be shared.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What controls preview when link shared on social? Not title alone, but OG protocol.
blocks.reasoning: Open Graph protocol (og:*) controls social sharing previews. Without them, platforms show plain URL.

blocks.question: You build FAQ with divs and JavaScript click handlers to show/hide answers. Senior dev says use details/summary instead. What are advantages of native details/summary over custom div+JS?
options: No advantage, div+JS is always better because details/summary is deprecated and doesn't work on mobile

Advantages: Native accessible by default with keyboard and screen reader announcing expanded/collapsed state, no JavaScript needed, open attribute controls default state, semantic meaning of disclosure widget, less code, better performance - while div+JS requires manual ARIA, keyboard handling, and more code
Advantages: details/summary loads faster because it's CSS not HTML, and div is slower because it's JavaScript
Advantages: Only that details/summary has default styling with arrow, div requires CSS for arrow
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect modern HTML5 knowledge! Native > custom when possible.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Think accessibility: Does div have built-in expanded state announcement? Does details?
blocks.reasoning: details/summary is native disclosure widget, accessible, semantic, no JS needed, keyboard support built-in.

blocks.question: You embed YouTube video with <iframe src="youtube.com/embed/..."></iframe> without title attribute. Accessibility audit fails it. Also video loads immediately slowing page. What are two fixes required for production complete webpage?
options: Add alt attribute to iframe for accessibility and add preload="none" to prevent immediate loading

Add title attribute describing embedded content for screen readers (mandatory for iframe accessibility) and add loading="lazy" to defer loading until near viewport, improving performance for complete webpage
Add aria-label to parent div and add autoplay="false" to prevent loading
Wrap iframe in <figure> and add <figcaption> for accessibility, and add width="0" to hide initially
blocks.correctFeedback: Excellent iframe production knowledge! Title and lazy loading are mandatory for modern webpages.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What does screen reader announce for iframe without title? How to defer loading?
blocks.reasoning: Iframe requires title for accessibility - describes embedded content. loading=lazy defers offscreen iframe loading, improving page speed.

blocks.question:
You add
Portfolio
and . Which statement about data-* and progress is correct for production complete webpage?
options: data-* is invalid HTML and should not be used, use class instead for storing data; progress max must be 100 not 1, value 0.8 is invalid

data-* attributes are valid way to store custom private data for JavaScript/CSS without non-standard attributes, accessible via dataset API; progress value can be 0.8 with max 1 or 80 with max 100 both valid representing 80%, but max must be positive number
data-* only works inside form elements not divs, and progress only works inside form, both invalid outside form
data-* requires data- prefix but value must be JSON string, so data-price="500" invalid should be data-price='{"value":500}'
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect! data-* and progress/meter are key for modern interactive webpages.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Is data-* valid on any element? What does progress value/max represent?
blocks.reasoning: data-* is standard for custom data on any element. progress value/max define completion ratio, can be fraction or integer, max must be >0.

You now know meta description and OG tags for WhatsApp rich preview, details/summary for FAQ without JS, dialog for modals, datalist for autocomplete, progress/meter/output for dashboards, iframe with title and lazy loading for maps/videos, entities for showing code, data attributes for JS, template for dynamic content.
